_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::input_format#0, rule confirmed and Signal corrected. meshio 5.3.5 writes a one-hex ExodusII mesh with eb_prop1=[0] and the netCDF4 patch (eb_prop1 += 1) turns it into [1]; 4C echoes exactly that as 'cell-block 0 ()' and 'cell-block 1 ()' in its mesh summary. Pointing ELEMENT_BLOCKS at ID: 1 against the unpatched meshio mesh produces NO 4C diagnostic at all — zero PROC 0 ERROR blocks, zero mentions of ELEMENT_BLOCKS / no elements / element block anywhere in the log — and the run dies later inside the linear solver with "terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'" and 'umfpack_solve has error code: -3', shell status 134. The claimed 'Pressure map empty' signal appears nowhere (0 occurrences). The only clue is the mesh-summary line disagreeing with the ID in the deck. Both correct spellings work and agree: ID: 0 against the meshio mesh and ID: 1 against the netCDF4-patched mesh each exit 0, pass the pinned dispy 4.47909266337460053e-03 at TOLERANCE 1e-12, and report the identical abs(diff) (FIX_REPRODUCES_THE_ANSWER=yes). Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev (git 89519cf) at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C.
expect_in_output: terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'

_mutation.note: remove the pathology: name the block id meshio actually wrote. The UMFPACK abort vanishes, EXIT_ID1MESHIO becomes 0, and the fixture must go red.

remove the recorded fix: stop patching eb_prop1 with netCDF4, so the 'patched' mesh is still 0-indexed. It then fails the same way the unpatched one does, EXIT_ID1PATCHED stops being 0, and the fixture must go red.
